title: Medicine, Convexity, and Opacity
coreMove: Intervene more readily when upside is convex and downside limited, and hesitate when hidden harm dominates.
sourcePressure: This chapter applies asymmetry and opacity to intervention-heavy domains, especially medicine-like systems.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reading the chapter as crude anti-medicine or anti-treatment rhetoric.

sourceAnchors.name: medicine-like systems
sourceAnchors.detail: the source notes point to opaque domains where intervention risk can be hidden
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: In an opaque body, the visible fix may not be the largest effect.

sourceAnchors.name: convexity
sourceAnchors.detail: the chapter asks whether response structure makes intervention favorable or dangerous
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Convexity tells you whether a small intervention can buy large upside without equal ruin.
